discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can turn an ordinary time-reversal-invariant insulator into a new quantum phase. This phase has a Z2 topological invariant and helical edge states that are protected against backscattering. It was the first topological phase that needs no magnetic field. Molenkamp's group gave the decisive experimental confirmation in 2007, measuring quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, as Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang had predicted. These results set off the field of topological insulators and superconductors and the tenfold classification of topological matter. They underlie today's searches for Majorana and parafermion bound states and for topologically protected quantum information. The theory is clean, the materials are concrete, and the signature is robust and quantized. This makes it a model of how theory and experiment together establish a new state of matter, beyond reasonable doubt.
